title: Why is yawning contagious? - Claudia Aguirre
speaker: TED-Ed
zh: 【TED-Ed】為什麼打哈欠會傳染？ ——克勞蒂亞·阿吉雷（精選雙語跟讀教材）

cues.text: Oh, excuse me!
cues.en: Oh, excuse me!
cues.zh: 不好意思！

cues.text: Have you ever yawned because somebody else yawned?
cues.en: Have you ever yawned because somebody else yawned?
cues.zh: 別人打哈欠 你會不會也打哈欠？

cues.text: You aren't especially tired, yet suddenly your mouth opens wide
cues.en: You aren't especially tired, yet suddenly your mouth opens wide
cues.zh: 其實沒有特別累 但突然就張大嘴巴

cues.text: and a big yawn comes out.
cues.en: and a big yawn comes out.
cues.zh: 一個大哈欠 就跑出來了

cues.text: This phenomenon is known as contagious yawning.
cues.en: This phenomenon is known as contagious yawning.
cues.zh: 這現象叫哈欠傳染

cues.text: And while scientists still don't fully understand why it happens, there are many hypotheses currently being researched.
cues.en: And while scientists still don't fully understand why it happens, there are many hypotheses currently being researched.
cues.zh: 對於背後的原因 科學家還不完全瞭解 但已經有人在研究各種假說

cues.text: Let's take a look at a few of the most prevalent ones, beginning with two physiological hypotheses
cues.en: Let's take a look at a few of the most prevalent ones, beginning with two physiological hypotheses
cues.zh: 讓我們來瞭解 一些廣為流傳的說法 先聽聽 2 種生理假說

cues.text: before moving to a psychological one.
cues.en: before moving to a psychological one.
cues.zh: 再看看 1 種心理假說

cues.text: Our first physiological hypothesis states that contagious yawning is triggered by a specific stimulus,
cues.en: Our first physiological hypothesis states that contagious yawning is triggered by a specific stimulus,
cues.zh: 第 1 種生理假說認為 哈欠傳染其來有自 會由特定刺激引起

cues.text: an initial yawn.
cues.en: an initial yawn.
cues.zh: 會由特定刺激引起 就是最初的哈欠

cues.text: This is called fixed action pattern.
cues.en: This is called fixed action pattern.
cues.zh: 就是最初的哈欠 這叫固定行為模式

cues.text: Think of fixed action pattern like a reflex.
cues.en: Think of fixed action pattern like a reflex.
cues.zh: 有點像反射動作

cues.text: Your yawn makes me yawn.
cues.en: Your yawn makes me yawn.
cues.zh: 有點像反射動作 你的哈欠讓我打哈欠

cues.text: Similar to a domino effect, one person's yawn triggers a yawn in a person nearby that has observed the act.
cues.en: Similar to a domino effect, one person's yawn triggers a yawn in a person nearby that has observed the act.
cues.zh: 你的哈欠讓我打哈欠 類似多米諾骨牌效應 一個人的哈欠 讓附近看到的人也打哈欠

cues.text: Once this reflex is triggered, it must run its course.
cues.en: Once this reflex is triggered, it must run its course.
cues.zh: 這效應一旦啟動 就會持續一定的時間

cues.text: Have you ever tried to stop a yawn once it has begun?
cues.en: Have you ever tried to stop a yawn once it has begun?
cues.zh: 快打哈欠時 你有試過阻止自己嗎？

cues.text: Basically impossible!
cues.en: Basically impossible!
cues.zh: 你有試過阻止自己嗎？ 根本不可能！

cues.text: Another physiological hypothesis is known as non-conscious mimicry,
cues.en: Another physiological hypothesis is known as non-conscious mimicry,
cues.zh: 第 2 種生理假說 叫無意識模仿

cues.text: or the chameleon effect.
cues.en: or the chameleon effect.
cues.zh: 又稱變色龍效應

cues.text: This occurs when you imitate someone's behavior without knowing it,
cues.en: This occurs when you imitate someone's behavior without knowing it,
cues.zh: 又稱變色龍效應 人會模仿他人的行為 下意識地 做出細微、自然的複製動作

cues.text: a subtle and unintentional copycat maneuver.
cues.en: a subtle and unintentional copycat maneuver.
cues.zh: 做出細微、自然的複製動作

cues.text: People tend to mimic each other's postures.
cues.en: People tend to mimic each other's postures.
cues.zh: 人會模仿他人的姿勢

cues.text: If you are seated across from someone that has their legs crossed,
cues.en: If you are seated across from someone that has their legs crossed,
cues.zh: 人會模仿他人的姿勢 像是對面的人翹腳 你看到了 很有可能也會翹起腳來

cues.text: you might cross your own legs.
cues.en: you might cross your own legs.
cues.zh: 很有可能也會翹起腳來

cues.text: This hypothesis suggests that we yawn when we see someone else yawn
cues.en: This hypothesis suggests that we yawn when we see someone else yawn
cues.zh: 這假說認為 看到別人打哈欠就跟進 是因為不知不覺中

cues.text: because we are unconsciously copying his or her behavior.
cues.en: because we are unconsciously copying his or her behavior.
cues.zh: 是因為不知不覺中 我們會模仿他人的行為

cues.text: Scientists believe that this chameleon effect is possible because of a special set of neurons known as mirror neurons.
cues.en: Scientists believe that this chameleon effect is possible because of a special set of neurons known as mirror neurons.
cues.zh: 科學家相信 變色龍效應可能和特殊的神經元有關 也就是映象神經元

cues.text: Mirror neurons are a type of brain cell that responds equally when we perform an action
cues.en: Mirror neurons are a type of brain cell that responds equally when we perform an action
cues.zh: 映象神經元是一群腦細胞 像鏡子一樣

cues.text: as when we see someone else perform the same action.
cues.en: as when we see someone else perform the same action.
cues.zh: 看到他人的動作後 我們會做出相同的動作

cues.text: These neurons are important for learning and self-awareness.
cues.en: These neurons are important for learning and self-awareness.
cues.zh: 這組神經元很重要 尤其對學習和自我覺察

cues.text: For example, watching someone do something physical, like knitting or putting on lipstick,
cues.en: For example, watching someone do something physical, like knitting or putting on lipstick,
cues.zh: 尤其對學習和自我覺察 例如，看到別人的動作 像是編織 或是擦口紅

cues.text: can help you do those same actions more accurately.
cues.en: can help you do those same actions more accurately.
cues.zh: 或是擦口紅 能讓我們精確地做出相同的動作

cues.text: Neuroimaging studies using fMRI, functional magnetic resonance imaging,
cues.en: Neuroimaging studies using fMRI, functional magnetic resonance imaging,
cues.zh: 腦神經影像利用醫學技術 也就是功能性核磁共振造影

cues.text: show us that when we seem someone yawn or even hear their yawn,
cues.en: show us that when we seem someone yawn or even hear their yawn,
cues.zh: 也就是功能性核磁共振造影 發現看到別人打哈欠 或只是聽到哈欠聲

cues.text: a specific area of the brain housing these mirror neurons tends to light up,
cues.en: a specific area of the brain housing these mirror neurons tends to light up,
cues.zh: 或只是聽到哈欠聲 我們腦中 有映象神經元的區塊 會有反應

cues.text: which, in turn, causes us to respond with the same action:
cues.en: which, in turn, causes us to respond with the same action:
cues.zh: 促使我們做出回應 重複相同的動作：打哈欠

cues.text: a yawn!
cues.en: a yawn!
cues.zh: 重複相同的動作：打哈欠

cues.text: Our psychological hypothesis also involves the work of these mirror neurons.
cues.en: Our psychological hypothesis also involves the work of these mirror neurons.
cues.zh: 最後要談的心理假說 也和映象神經元有關 稱為同理哈欠

cues.text: We will call it the empathy yawn.
cues.en: We will call it the empathy yawn.
cues.zh: 稱為同理哈欠

cues.text: Empathy is the ability to understand what someone else is feeling and partake in their emotion,
cues.en: Empathy is the ability to understand what someone else is feeling and partake in their emotion,
cues.zh: 同理心是種能力 能感知他人的感受 融入對方的情緒 對人這種社會性動物很重要

cues.text: a crucial ability for social animals like us.
cues.en: a crucial ability for social animals like us.
cues.zh: 對人這種社會性動物很重要

cues.text: Recently, neuroscientists have found that a subset of mirror neurons
cues.en: Recently, neuroscientists have found that a subset of mirror neurons
cues.zh: 近來，神經學家發現 映象神經元有組子集

cues.text: allows us to empathize with others' feelings at a deeper level.
cues.en: allows us to empathize with others' feelings at a deeper level.
cues.zh: 映象神經元有組子集 能讓我們同理他人 而且是深層同理

cues.text: Scientists discovered this empathetic response to yawning while testing the first hypothesis we mentioned,
cues.en: Scientists discovered this empathetic response to yawning while testing the first hypothesis we mentioned,
cues.zh: 事實上 同理哈欠現象 是在測試固定行為時 所發現的

cues.text: fixed action pattern.
cues.en: fixed action pattern.
cues.zh: 所發現的 這研究假設

cues.text: This study was set up to show that dogs would enact a yawn reflex
cues.en: This study was set up to show that dogs would enact a yawn reflex
cues.zh: 這研究假設 如果狗聽到人類打哈欠

cues.text: at the mere sound of a human yawn.
cues.en: at the mere sound of a human yawn.
cues.zh: 也會反射性地打起哈欠

cues.text: While their study showed this to be true, they found something else interesting.
cues.en: While their study showed this to be true, they found something else interesting.
cues.zh: 不僅證實了這種現象 還發現了其他有趣的事

cues.text: Dogs yawned more frequently at familiar yawns, such as from their owners,
cues.en: Dogs yawned more frequently at familiar yawns, such as from their owners,
cues.zh: 熟人的哈欠對狗比較有影響力 像是主人

cues.text: than at unfamiliar yawns from strangers.
cues.en: than at unfamiliar yawns from strangers.
cues.zh: 但對陌生人就不是了

cues.text: Following this research, other studies on humans and primates have also shown that contagious yawning
cues.en: Following this research, other studies on humans and primates have also shown that contagious yawning
cues.zh: 同樣地 以人類和靈長類為研究物件 也證實哈欠傳染 在熟人間發生的機率高於陌生人

cues.text: occurs more frequently among friends than strangers.
cues.en: occurs more frequently among friends than strangers.
cues.zh: 在熟人間發生的機率高於陌生人

cues.text: In fact, contagious yawning starts occurring when we are about four or five years old,
cues.en: In fact, contagious yawning starts occurring when we are about four or five years old,
cues.zh: 事實上，早在4、5 歲時 對哈欠傳染就有反應了

cues.text: at the point when children develop the ability to identify others' emotions properly.
cues.en: at the point when children develop the ability to identify others' emotions properly.
cues.zh: 對哈欠傳染就有反應了 那時 兒童開始能正確瞭解他人的情緒

cues.text: Still, while newer scientific studies aim to prove that contagious yawning
cues.en: Still, while newer scientific studies aim to prove that contagious yawning
cues.zh: 儘管相關研究推陳出新 想證明哈欠傳染的產生 是因為同理能力

cues.text: is based on this capacity for empathy, more research is needed to shed light on what exactly is going on.
cues.en: is based on this capacity for empathy, more research is needed to shed light on what exactly is going on.
cues.zh: 是因為同理能力 但其實 更需要研究的是背後的機制

cues.text: It's possible that the answer lies in another hypothesis altogether.
cues.en: It's possible that the answer lies in another hypothesis altogether.
cues.zh: 說不定真正的答案 就藏在其他假說裡

cues.text: The next time you get caught in a yawn, take a second to think about what just happened.
cues.en: The next time you get caught in a yawn, take a second to think about what just happened.
cues.zh: 下次打哈欠時 停下來想想剛才的情形

cues.text: Were you thinking about a yawn?
cues.en: Were you thinking about a yawn?
cues.zh: 是不是想到了哈欠這件事？

cues.text: Did someone near you yawn?
cues.en: Did someone near you yawn?
cues.zh: 附近有人打哈欠嗎？

cues.text: Was that person a stranger or someone close?
cues.en: Was that person a stranger or someone close?
cues.zh: 附近有人打哈欠嗎？ 是熟人？還是陌生人？

cues.text: And are you yawning right now?
cues.en: And are you yawning right now?
cues.zh: 你現在在打哈欠嗎？
